narrative:
The model determined that you have a 36% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeded the bank's acceptance threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, how long you have lived at your current residence, and the length of the loan you requested. Your checking account status was the single biggest reason for the denial. Having between 0 and 200 DM in your account is relatively uncommon among approved applicants and pushed the prediction noticeably toward bad credit risk. In contrast, the fact that you have lived at your present address for only one year worked in your favor; shorter residence times are associated with lower risk in the model and therefore pulled the prediction back toward approval. Finally, requesting a 12-month loan also helped your case. Most approved applicants ask for almost 20 months, so your shorter duration reduced the predicted risk.

Even though two of the top factors worked in your favor, the negative signal from your checking account proved decisive. 

To improve your chances next time, focus on building a healthier balance in your checking account before reapplying. This single change would likely have the largest positive impact on future decisions. Consider waiting until you can show a more stable financial footprint, then submit a new application.
